doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: A Closer Walk and Phil Harris at the club
summary: A caller praises Pete's A Closer Walk; Pete says it and The Saints are nightly standards, and mentions Phil Harris.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Bye. Hello. Go ahead, please. Okay.
I wanted to talk to, I'll give Pete a little talk to. Is he listening?
Right.
Okay, Pete.
Yeah.
I'm no musician or anything, but a few years ago when you played the Closer Walk, I really enjoyed it.
At the game?
The song, the Closer Walk?
Yeah. Was that at the game when I did it with the grambling band?
No, this was probably 15 years ago when I was in Jacksonville, Florida.
Oh.
And so I always wanted to, you know, so about a year ago, my wife and I came to your club, and sure enough, you played it there.
Yeah, we usually play it every night. It's been like a standard with us. That and the Saints, we have to do it, or they throw tomatoes at me or something.
Well, you really do a good job of it.
Thank you, sir.
The night we was at the club, your old buddy, Phil Harris, was there.
Oh, well, he and I do a pretty good job with the Jack Daniels.
I do myself.
Wonderful.
Okay, it's been a pleasure talking to you.
